question.problem:
The diastolic blood pressure of a group of people is normally distributed with a mean of $85\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and a standard deviation of $14\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected person from the group has a diastolic blood pressure greater than $77\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and less than $86\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}?$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2546\,$ $\,0.2514\,$ $\,0.2483\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.2877\,$ $\,0.2843\,$ $\,0.2810\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3228\,$ $\,0.3192\,$ $\,0.3156\,$
$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4364\,$ $\,0.4325\,$ $\,0.4286\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5239\,$ $\,0.5279\,$ $\,0.5319\,$
$\,0.1\,$ $\,0.5636\,$ $\,0.5675\,$ $\,0.5714\,$
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the diastolic blood pressure of the selected person. Then we have $X∼N(85,{14}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(77<X<86).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(77<X<86) & =P(\frac{77-85}{14}<Z<\frac{86-85}{14}) \\  & =P(-0.57<Z<0.07)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.57<Z<0.07) & =P(Z<0.07)-P(Z\le -0.57) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.07)-P(Z\le -0.57) \\  & =Φ(0.07)-Φ(-0.57)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.07) & =0.5279 \\ Φ(-0.57) & =0.2843\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.57<Z<0.07) & =Φ(0.07)-Φ(-0.57) \\  & =0.5279-0.2843 \\  & =0.2436.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the randomly selected person from the group has a diastolic blood pressure greater than $77\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ and less than $86\,\text{mm}\,\text{Hg}$ is approximately $0.24.$
